DVDs, TV recordings and 1080i broadcasts can show jagged comb lines around moving objects. Deinterlacing smooths them out when a video is decoded in software. Hardware decoders usually take care of it on their own.

resources.string: Movies are 24 frames per second. When your screen speed fits that exactly, motion is already perfectly even. Smooth motion works with both the Vulkan and OpenGL renderers.
Shows each frame as it is. Slow pans can stutter a little on 60 Hz and 90 Hz screens
Blends only the moment when frames change. Every frame stays crisp and stutter is reduced
Blends on every screen refresh for perfectly even motion. Fast scenes can look slightly ghosted
Switches your screen to a speed that fits the video only if it can do it without blinking
Always switches to a speed that fits the video. The screen may blink once when playback starts
Creates real in-between frames by tracking motion in the video, so movement looks truly fluid. Uses more GPU power
Higher quality tracks motion more precisely but needs a stronger GPU.
Measures your device and picks the best quality it can keep up with
Coarse motion tracking, lightest on the GPU. Good for budget phones
Finer tracking with cleaner edges. Good for most phones
Finest tracking with extra edge checks. For phones with strong GPUs
Higher rates look smoother but use more battery. Only rates your screen supports are used.
Where motion can’t be tracked reliably, blend frames instead of risking halos or warping.
Keeps two different shots from morphing into each other. Higher catches more cuts.
Skips repeated drawings so animation flows between the real ones
Interpolate only videos at 30 fps or less
Turn interpolation off while battery saver is on
Lower the quality when your phone warms up, and turn it off if it gets too hot
Softens loud scenes and lifts quiet dialogue so you can keep the volume low
Makes voices clearer over music and effects
Keeps loud and quiet scenes closer to the same level, and uses a file’s ReplayGain tags when it has them. Audio passthrough is paused while this is on.
Pick a preset or drag the bands to shape the sound.
Lucky decodes every audio format itself, so DTS, Dolby, FLAC and Opus play on any phone.

Auto keeps surround sound, up to 7.1, when the connected output can play it, such as HDMI or a USB audio device. Phone speakers and Bluetooth always get a stereo mix. Stereo downmixes everything to two channels.
Falls back to normal decoding while speed or sound effects are on

When your receiver or TV can decode the format, Lucky sends it the original AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, DTS-HD or TrueHD sound untouched. While playback speed isn’t 1×, or the equalizer, volume boost, night mode, dialogue boost, balance or channel mode is on, Lucky decodes the audio itself instead, since none of those can be applied to untouched audio.
Used for the play button, the seek bar and buttons that are turned on.
